data.title: The Call Guaranty Trust Bulls Got Right
data.description:
Guaranty Trust just delivered a result that jars with its latest financials. Revenue and profit were lower in Q3 2026 than a year earlier and net margin also slipped, yet the reward for staying in the stock was anything but modest. Investors who held Guaranty Trust over the past year are up 49.2%, including dividends. If you had been deciding in November 2025, how would you have weighed that eventual payoff against the clear risks around HabariPay, regulation and capital raising?

A Narrative on Simply Wall St is one investor's written case for a company, with its growth, margin and multiple assumptions spelled out. Those assumptions imply an estimated Fair Value.

Guaranty Trust has already moved. See which of 195 high quality undervalued stocks still trade below our estimates.

The Two Guaranty Trust Stories Investors Were Weighing

The shares cost NGN85.8 at the start of the period, so any holder in Guaranty Trust had to decide which story felt more convincing.

On the optimistic side, one narrative put Fair Value at NGN91.91, about 7% above the start price. It leaned on assumptions like 26.2% revenue growth and a 52.8% profit margin over a 3 year window, helped by HabariPay and East Africa expansion.

The cautious view pointed to NGN68.38 as Fair Value, roughly 20% below the start price. That argument focused on digital only banks, tougher regulation in Nigeria and the risk that funding could become more restrictive.

What The Results Changed For The Guaranty Trust Debate

The clearest fresh fact on Guaranty Trust is the Q3 2026 report. Revenue slipped from NGN406,396m in Q3 2025 to NGN399,285.354m and net income declined, with net margin compressing from 60.7% to 49.5%. That pattern challenged the more optimistic case that leaned on very high profitability and upbeat growth assumptions.

The takeaway for other banks is simple. When a thesis leans on expanding profitability, treat net margin as the key claimant and check later filings to see whether that specific ratio is moving in the direction the story assumed.

What Guaranty Trust's Run Now Asks You To Believe

Guaranty Trust trades at NGN120 today after a 49.2% gain over the past year, and this Narrative's Fair Value still sits above that level rather than below it.

The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St leans on how Guaranty Trust deploys its enlarged capital base, payments engine and non banking arms. The question is whether disciplined loan growth and HabariPay funded deposits really can keep supporting that thesis.

"The capital that Guaranty Trust Holding recently raised has been only partly deployed, with about 60% already directed into technology, branch expansion in markets such as Ghana and Nigeria, and working capital, which leaves a sizeable pool still to be allocated into loans and investment securities that could support revenue and earnings. The push to grow loans by around 25% using a mix of corporate, retail and SME lending, while actively flexing between placements, investment securities and loans based on pricing and risk, is intended to protect net interest margin and support future interest income rather than chase volume at the expense of asset quality."

Looking Beyond Guaranty Trust

Guaranty Trust keeps pulling attention to margin debates and capital use. Just beside that discussion, a different kind of banking question emerges.

Large universal banks are wrestling with a similar challenge. They still need to turn vast deposit pools into steadier fee and wealth income.

One global player is leaning harder on digital tools and AI. It wants to deepen existing relationships instead of chasing flashier products.

The same bank is also pushing further into cross border banking and payments. If that mix of technology, deposits and international reach connects effectively, the earnings shape could shift meaningfully.

data.title: santec Holdings' (TSE:6777) Earnings Are Weaker Than They Seem
data.description:
santec Holdings Corporation's (TSE:6777) stock was strong after they recently reported robust earnings. However, we think that shareholders may be missing some concerning details in the numbers.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Zooming In On santec Holdings' Earnings

As finance nerds would already know, the accrual ratio from cashflow is a key measure for assessing how well a company's free cash flow (FCF) matches its profit. In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. You could think of the accrual ratio from cashflow as the 'non-FCF profit ratio'.

Therefore, it's actually considered a good thing when a company has a negative accrual ratio, but a bad thing if its accrual ratio is positive. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

santec Holdings has an accrual ratio of 0.27 for the year to September 2026. Therefore, we know that it's free cashflow was significantly lower than its statutory profit, which is hardly a good thing. In fact, it had free cash flow of JP¥6.4b in the last year, which was a lot less than its statutory profit of JP¥10.7b. At this point we should mention that santec Holdings did manage to increase its free cash flow in the last twelve months

Our Take On santec Holdings' Profit Performance

santec Holdings didn't convert much of its profit to free cash flow in the last year, which some investors may consider rather suboptimal. data.title: Investors Shouldn't Be Too Comfortable With TOA's (TSE:6809) Earnings
data.description:
TOA Corporation (TSE:6809) announced strong profits, but the stock was stagnant. We did some digging, and we found some concerning factors in the details.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

To understand the value of a company's earnings growth, it is imperative to consider any dilution of shareholders' interests. In fact, TOA increased the number of shares on issue by 15% over the last twelve months by issuing new shares. That means its earnings are split among a greater number of shares. To celebrate net income while ignoring dilution is like rejoicing because you have a single slice of a larger pizza, but ignoring the fact that the pizza is now cut into many more slices. Check out TOA's historical EPS growth by clicking on this link.

How Is Dilution Impacting TOA's Earnings Per Share (EPS)?

TOA has improved its profit over the last three years, with an annualized gain of 131% in that time. And at a glance the 42% gain in profit over the last year impresses. On the other hand, earnings per share are only up 27% in that time. Therefore, the dilution is having a noteworthy influence on shareholder returns.

Changes in the share price do tend to reflect changes in earnings per share, in the long run. So it will certainly be a positive for shareholders if TOA can grow EPS persistently. But on the other hand, we'd be far less excited to learn profit (but not EPS) was improving. For the ordinary retail shareholder, EPS is a great measure to check your hypothetical "share" of the company's profit.

Note: we always recommend investors check balance sheet strength. Click here to be taken to our balance sheet analysis of TOA.

Our Take On TOA's Profit Performance

Each TOA share now gets a meaningfully smaller slice of its overall profit, due to dilution of existing shareholders. Therefore, it seems possible to us that TOA's true underlying earnings power is actually less than its statutory profit. But on the bright side, its earnings per share have grown at an extremely impressive rate over the last three years. At the end of the day, it's essential to consider more than just the factors above, if you want to understand the company properly. Keep in mind, when it comes to analysing a stock it's worth noting the risks involved. While conducting our analysis, we found that TOA has 2 warning signs and it would be unwise to ignore these bad boys.

This note has only looked at a single factor that sheds light on the nature of TOA's profit. But there are plenty of other ways to inform your opinion of a company. data.title: Moderna (MRNA) Lands New Vaccine Data Win And Global Index Inclusion
data.description:

  • The same study found mNEXSPIKE was associated with lower COVID 19 related hospitalizations for older adults compared with a major competitor vaccine.
  • MSCI plans to add Moderna to the MSCI World Index, increasing the stock's visibility for global and index tracking investors.
  • The mNEXSPIKE effectiveness data and MSCI World Index inclusion are important, but they do not capture everything shaping Moderna's outlook. We have also spotted 1 major warning sign worth knowing about at Moderna.

The Moderna Narrative says the stock is really a bet that an mRNA platform can support a wide vaccines, oncology and rare disease portfolio rather than a single COVID line, and this real world data plus MSCI World Index inclusion both touch that thesis directly.

"The build out of Moderna’s multi product vaccine portfolio, with five approved products and two additional launches planned for 2026, can encourage investors to extrapolate a long runway for respiratory and other infectious disease vaccine revenue and assign a rich P/S multiple to that future top line..."

For investors who already viewed COVID demand as fading quickly, that is an important signal rather than just another trial readout.

Index inclusion hits a different nerve in the Narrative. A stock entering the MSCI World Index tends to draw more attention from global and index tracking investors.
